blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Most tax problems come from a small number of common mistakes. You miss a deadline. You lose an invoice. You classify an expense in the wrong way. You confuse personal and business costs. Or you forget a new rule the tax office announced last month.

If any of these happens, the penalty is usually small the first time. But it gets bigger each time it repeats. The tax office is much more forgiving of honest, well-documented errors than of the same error happening three years in a row.

The lesson is simple. When you spot a mistake, fix it quickly. Write down what you did. And make sure the same mistake cannot happen again next month.

items.q: Where do most tax problems come from?
options: A small number of common mistakes
items.why: "Most tax problems come from a small number of common mistakes."

items.q: What happens to the penalty each time the same mistake repeats?
items.why: "the penalty is usually small the first time. But it gets bigger each time it repeats."

items.q: The text says the tax office is more forgiving of…
options: the same error three years in a row
items.why: "more forgiving of honest, well-documented errors than of the same error happening three years in a row."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: It is fine to make the same mistake every year.
You should fix a mistake quickly.
Writing down what you did is a good idea.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo diz o contrário — repetir o mesmo erro é o que traz multas maiores.

items.q: "Make sure the same mistake cannot happen again next month" suggests that…
options: you should change the process, not just fix one case
items.why: Inferência: prevenir a repetição significa mudar como o trabalho é feito, não só corrigir uma vez.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte falando com o novo colega júnior. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Good morning. Today we look at last year's compliance errors. Do not worry — this is normal. Every company makes some mistakes. Our job is to learn from them.

I counted all the errors from last year. Here is the interesting part. Eighty percent of them came from just five types of mistake. Only five. A missed deadline. A lost invoice. A wrong expense classification. Personal and business costs mixed together. And a new rule that someone forgot.

So this is good news for us. If we fix these five things, we remove most of the problem. We do not need a hundred new rules. We need five good habits.

Here is my advice, and it is very simple. When you see a mistake, tell me the same day. Do not wait, and do not hide it. We fix it together, we write a short note, and then we change the process. If we do that, the same mistake will not come back next month. That is the goal. Small errors are fine — we all make them. Repeated errors are the real problem. Any questions before we start?
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What are Charlotte and the junior looking at today?
items.why: "Today we look at last year's compliance errors."

items.q: How much of the errors came from just five types of mistake?
items.why: "Eighty percent of them came from just five types of mistake."

items.q: What does Charlotte want the junior to do when he sees a mistake?
options: Fix it alone and say nothing
Send it to the tax office
Wait until the end of the month
items.why: "When you see a mistake, tell me the same day."

items.q: Why does Charlotte say this is "good news"?
options: Because the tax office will pay them
Because fixing five things removes most of the problem
Because they need a hundred new rules
items.why: Inferência: se poucos erros causam quase tudo, resolver esses poucos resolve a maior parte.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's tone with the junior?
items.why: Inferência: ela diz "do not worry" e propõe hábitos simples — tom tranquilo e de apoio.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We must send the report before the deadline." A deadline is…
options: the last day or time to do something
items.why: Deadline = prazo, a data-limite para entregar algo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please do not ___ the invoice — we need it for the tax office."
items.why: To lose = perder; o texto pede para não perder a nota fiscal.

items.q: "You must classify each cost correctly." To classify means to…
options: put into the right group or type
items.why: To classify = classificar, colocar cada item no grupo certo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Lunch with a friend is not a business ___."
items.why: Expense = despesa; um almoço pessoal não é despesa da empresa.

items.q: "If we repeat the same error, we pay a bigger penalty." A penalty is…
items.why: Penalty = multa, o valor que se paga por um erro.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the tax report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval final.

items.q: "When you find a mistake, please write it down." To write down means to…
items.why: Write down = anotar, registrar por escrito.

items.q: "We need to keep up with new tax rules." To keep up with means to…
items.why: Keep up with = acompanhar, ficar por dentro.

items.q: "The junior agreed to help but did not follow through." This means he…
options: did not finish what he agreed to do
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's sort out this error today." To sort out means to…
items.why: Sort out = resolver, colocar em ordem.
